title: Need Help with 2D Character Rigging and Walk Animations in a Darkest Dungeon-Style Web Game
author: kev1n53
selftext: Hi everyone, I’m building a 2D game inspired by Darkest Dungeon using Claude Code. Right now it’s running in the browser, but I’m planning to move it to Godot and later release on Android. I’m struggling with character rigging and walk animations. Clothing and body parts don’t follow the skeleton correctly, and the walk animation just breaks. What’s the best approach for 2D skeletal animations if I start on web but plan to move to Godot? Should I look into Spine, Rive, Godot’s Skeleton2D, or something else? Any tips or examples would be amazing. Thanks!

comments.author: forgetscode
comments.body:
People have opinions. The truth is AI models aren't very good at these types of things today. You're better off sticking to things they are good at and then they'll probably be good at this too within a few months. 

it will be pretty painstaking to make something polished with this approach today but it definitely is possible. you'll need to constantly correct mistakes no matter how good you document.

My recommendation, ask Claude code to animate with code in a style it's good to create animations then tell it to use codex/imagen to create puppet pieces to put onto the code generated animation. kind of like a stick man then pasting stickers on them. Hands are very difficult for the model to understand.

My actual recommendation if you want to build something good like this. just build out your game assuming everything as placeholders using things Claude code is good at and focus on making a good game. When AI gets good enough to do what you want then make the upgrade and you'll be further along.

you can go a lot further letting models work on what they're good at rather than trying to force fit the shoe.
